result.title: Intuition with Evidence: Adaptive Dual Memory for Multimodal Agents
result.summary: As multimodal agents engage in sustained interactions, long-term memory serves two distinct but complementary functions: fine-grained evidence recall and internalized interpretation for global understanding. Although episodic and latent memory address these demands through explicit historical records and internalized experience, neither paradigm alone can accommodate the diverse memory affinities across tasks, owing to limitations in episodic evidence coverage and integration, and in latent factual grounding. To bridge this divide, we propose a dual-memory framework, unifying a model-native latent memory as an intuitive prior with a multi-indexed episodic memory for exact evidence reconstruction via retrieval-conditioned joint alignment. At inference, the framework adaptively composes these memories through a training-free routing mechanism driven by Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) sensitivity and confidence proxies for query-dependent memory affinity. Extensive evaluations across multimodal benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, outperforming single-paradigm baselines overall (+4.67\% over vanilla Episodic), with further analysis highlighting episodic strengths in evidence-localized tasks and latent contributions to integrating dispersed information and compensating for imperfect retrieval.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向多模态智能体的双记忆框架，把模型原生的 latent memory 当作直觉先验，与多索引 episodic memory 的证据重建能力结合，并在推理时用基于 JSD 敏感度与置信度的免训练路由自适应组合两者。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及 latent 内部化表示与显式视觉证据之间的取舍；其路由机制可供核查 latent 内容是否真正承担证据筛选与整合，以及检索不完善时的补偿关系。
